text:
Alex: Hey team — customer 'Clearport' just opened a P1. They say embeddings generated from our Hosted API vs their Dedicated cluster are coming back with different vector dims (1536 vs 1530). Happening only when they switch traffic from hosted -> dedicated. Reported for rw-embed-v2. Request id from hosted: req_h_01G3XJ9A, dedicated: req_d_01G3Y4KZ.

Rachel: ack, sorry they're hitting this in prod. Quick Qs: is this across all payloads or specific inputs? Any batching differences?

Alex: They sent a batch of mixed-length strings. On hosted they use batch_size=8 automatic batching, on Dedicated they run a client-side batch loop pushing 64 at a time through our route. They say dim mismatch sometimes and other times dims align.

Maria: That points at a serialization/packing bug. Two quick hypotheses: 1) partial truncation of last vector when the response stream is chunked; 2) alternate model variant (quantized kernel) being routed on Dedicated.

SRE Oncall: Can we get the raw responses for the two request ids? Also please paste the x-deployment-name header from the Dedicated request (we need exact model binary).

Alex: Pasting here from customer payloads (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, x-deployment-name: dedicated-pool-12, Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"model":"rw-embed-v2","inputs":["login error","how to reset password","referral program","pricing"... total 64 strings], "batch_size":64}
```
Response snippet (dedicated):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.00123, ... 1530 values ...]}, {"embedding":[0.00456, ... 1530 values ...}], ... , {"embedding":null}]}
```
Hosted response (same inputs):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.00123, ... 1536 values ...]}, ... ]}
```

Rachel: Interesting that one entry is null in the Dedicated response — that smells like a streaming/flush race where the vector write is truncated before closing the array. Do logs show any 5xx or connection reset around req_d_01G3Y4KZ?

InfraBot: Alert: deployment dedicated-pool-12 reported an I/O timeout to blob store at 2027-11-03T14:12:16Z for model rw-embed-v2-kernel-q8.

Maria: That confirms a resource-level blip. If a worker process tried to stream a vector and failed mid-write, JSON could be left malformed or we might return a partial array. But the API should never return wrong-dimension arrays; there should be a validation step.

SRE Oncall: Routine checks: 1) fetch model binary hash for dedicated-pool-12 in the last 24h; 2) check rollout history (did we fallback to q8 variant?); 3) check the response middleware that validates embedding length before sending. I'll run logs.

Alex: Customer also reported increased latency on Dedicated around same window (p95 spiking from 80ms to 900ms). Could be autoscaler thrash + batch size 64 causing OOM/queueing.

Rachel: For repro — Maria, can you try the following on a staging Dedicated cluster? Use a synthetic batch of 64 inputs, but interleave one very long input (10k chars) and one empty string to stress the batching and tokenizer. Use the exact route and headers:
```
curl -X POST https://dedicated.example.internal/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "x-deployment-name: dedicated-pool-12" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-embed-v2","inputs":["short","", "<10k chars>"], "batch_size":64}'
```
Goal: see if any embedding entries come back null or with wrong dims.

Maria: Running now on staging with q8 kernel and q4 kernel variants pinned. First run (q8): got one null embedding and one response with 1530 dims. Second run (q4): all 1536 dims. So it's kernel/quantization related.

Alex: So hypothesis: quantized kernel (q8) has a bug where under high batch sizes or when I/O stalls, output tensor gets truncated or kennel serializer uses a wrong fixed-length and strips trailing dims.

Rachel: OK actionable list: 1) hotfix: add server-side validation to drop or error on embeddings with length != expected and return 5xx instead of partial/invalid payload (safer than silent mismatch). 2) short-term: ask the customer to lower client batch_size to 8 for Dedicated while we root-cause. 3) longer-term: fix kernel serializer in q8 path.

SRE Oncall: I'll open an incident and attach logs and core dumps from dedicated-pool-12. Also will temporarily route traffic off dedicated-pool-12 for the customer's allocation (we can create a filter in routing policy).

InfraBot: Deploy note: a canary of rw-embed-v2-kernel-q8 was rolled to dedicated-pool-12 2027-11-02T02:04:22Z. No automated rollback triggered.

Maria: Additional repro detail: the wrong-dim vectors always end up 6 dims short (1536-1530 == 6). That pattern suggests off-by-N buffer trim during float->int8 packing or when trimming trailing zeros in a binary blob. I'll instrument serializer to log expected vs written length.

Alex: Customer response: temporary mitigation (batch_size 8) helped — they saw no dims mismatch in last 3 hours but p95 still slightly high. They've accepted a scheduled maintenance window to move traffic to another pool.

Rachel: I'll prepare the rollback and a communication note: explain that a quantized kernel variant exhibited intermittent truncation under certain batching/IO conditions, recommend short-term settings, and promise patch + validation added to the API.

SRE Oncall: Next steps assigned: Maria (kernel serializer logs + patch), Infra (route customer away from dedicated-pool-12), Rachel (customer comms + billing protection if they request credits), Alex (collect all repro artifacts and customer approval for maintenance). I'll file the incident with severity P1 and link this thread.

Support Bot: Ticket #44721 updated: customer agreed to maintenance at 2027-11-04T02:00Z. Support flow: please add a note to ticket mentioning batch_size mitigation and that we will protect them from overage billing during incident window.

Alex: Copy. I'll follow up with the customer and paste repro artifacts once Maria posts logs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
